“So they rolled away the heavy stone. Jesus gazed into heaven and said, “Father, thank you that you have heard my prayer, for you listen to every word I speak. Now, so that these who stand here with me will believe that you have sent me to the earth as your messenger, I will use the power you have given me.” Then with a loud voice Jesus shouted with authority: “Lazarus! Come out of the tomb!” Then in front of everyone, Lazarus, who had died four days earlier, slowly hobbled out—he still had grave clothes tightly wrapped around his hands and feet and covering his face! Jesus said to them, “Unwrap him and let him loose.” From that day forward many of those who had come to visit Mary believed in him, for they had seen with their own eyes this amazing miracle! John 11:41-45 (TPT). Oh Hallelujah. Beloved, the word of the Lord is true and absolute. 
Don’t look at the challenges to doubt God. 
Make the Word of the Lord your focus, and you will see the manifestation of His glory. Shalom!DIG DEEPER(John 11; Hebrews 11) WE PRAYThat no matter the opposition which will confront us, we shall not cast away our confidence in God and that we will remain resolute and indefatigable to work towards the Kingdom goals or targets given us. BIBLE READING IN THE YEAR 20261 YEAR PLAN Ezekiel 30–32 2 YEARS PLAN Song of Solomon 7 DECLARE THESE WORDS:– My time of harvest is here and I don’t permit any distraction from the adversary. – I refuse to doubt God, I hold on strongly to what God has said. – No challenge is big enough to move me away from God. – I don’t permit any voice to distract me from the sure word of God. – I imbue focus to maintain absolute confidence in God. – Through prayer and the study of the word I build more absolute confidence in God. – I don’t give my mind to the negative situations around me, I make the word of God my focus. Oh Hallelujah, Gloreeeey!!!

title: EPISODE 1329 - THE GOD-KIND OF EARLY SUCCESS
content:
CHRIST COMMONWEALTH-COMMUNITY The Love-Life Agency Download PDF Avoid any reason or anything that leads to idleness or unproductivity. Beloved, deal with laziness and rise. Selah. Apostle Bennie Author Saturday, 12th September, 2026  THE GOD-KIND OF EARLY SUCCESS“Oh, satisfy us early with Your mercy, That we may rejoice and be glad all our days!”  Psalm 90:14 (NKJV) You can be satisfied in your labour at the dawn or morning of your life. You don’t have to struggle through life till old age before you experience success. You can have the God-kind of success early. Take note, God-centered success or God kind of success, is not necessarily about the possession of material things. It is not the car you drive, the house you’ve bought, or the amount of money in your bank account. The God-kind of success is achieving God’s plan for you within a particular season. To have early success is to step into the fullness of your calling or purpose. It is making a tangible impact in the lives of people through the mandate the Lord has given you. Most people who don’t experience early success in the Kingdom, are often people who were busy with the pursuit of their own desires until they finally find the need to turn to God and follow His direction.
If you want to experience God early then you must seek Him early.
“O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is; To see thy power and thy glory, so as I have seen thee in the sanctuary. Because thy lovingkindness is better than life, my lips shall praise thee. Thus will I bless thee while I live: I will lift up my hands in thy name. My soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness; and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips“ Psalm 63:1-5 (KJV) Your early season to seek God is now. It takes a lot of steadfastness to grow into the assignment of God for your life. There are no “shortcuts”, you can’t jump the process. There is no sudden success. Jesus didn’t just wake up to use the last three (3) years of His life to accomplish these great results. He spent the first 30 years of His life preparing and building up to His purpose. There are about 11 years between Paul’s conversion (in Acts 9:1-9) and when he and Barnabas were separated by the Holy Spirit to their unique assignment the Lord has set for them. Paul the apostle didn’t just step into the scene to accomplish the things which he did. David didn’t just receive boldness overnight to defeat Goliath. According to the testimony of David to Saul, just as Goliath has been trained for war since childhood, he (David) was also prepared by God through several experiences as a shepherd boy. David learnt early in his life to deliver any of his lamb from a lion or bear as a shepherd. Therefore He had that same confidence that the Lord would help him deliver Israel out of the hands of Goliath and the army of the Philistines. (1 Samuel 17:34-36). Before this moment, David had learnt to defend what had been entrusted to him. He was always ready for the victory against Goliath.
You cannot have early success when you don’t know how to make the most of every opportunity the Lord bring your way.
Don’t waste time! Set your affection on the Lord. Set your focus on the Lord and His assignment for your life.  Stay committed to it now. Continue to serve the Lord’s purpose for your life. Be determined and diligent to accomplish the targets or goals given to you by the Lord. And you will begin to see the satisfaction of success. Shalom! DIG DEEPER(Psalm 90:12-17; Romans 13:11; Psalm 37:18-19; Ecclesiastes 9:12; Job 36:11) WE PRAYWe pray that we shall make the Lord our focus and pursue His purpose now, so that we shall experience early success. BIBLE READING IN THE YEAR 20261 YEAR PLAN Ezekiel 33–36 2 YEARS PLAN Song of Solomon 8 Isaiah 1 DECLARE THESE WORDS:– I incline my heart to the wisdom of God. – Through the wisdom of God, I make the most of every opportunity to have early success. – I make daily progress and success. – I make each day count. Thank you Lord Jesus!

title: EPISODE 1330 - LIVE ABOVE ALL LIMITATIONS
content:
CHRIST COMMONWEALTH-COMMUNITY The Love-Life Agency Download PDF What you accept as your revelation becomes the definition of your estate. Refuse stagnation, refuse failure, refuse unfruitfulness. Make a decision today that you are redeeming the times. Make the most of every opportunity now, to experience early success. Shalom! Apostle Bennie Author Sunday, 13th September, 2026 LIVE ABOVE ALL LIMITATIONS “And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” Genesis 27:40 (KJV) After Jacob had received all his father’s blessings, Esau returned to receive his father’s blessings, and there was nothing left for him. After much tears and pleading, Isaac spoke these words over Esau: “And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above; And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” Genesis 27:39-40 (KJV) Though Jacob has taken all the blessings and shall be lord over Esau, and Esau will also be a servant to Jacob, Isaac left Esau with a little window of hope. “and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck” Isaac showed Esau how he can break the yoke of limitations or slavery: When you shall have the dominion. Very few people have focused on these words of Isaac to Esau. Obviously, Esau’s decisions contributed to how he lost the blessing of the birthright. He technically traded his birthright as a firstborn for a single meal. Esau took the future for granted and focused on the present gratification. He lived carnally. The scriptures referred to him as godless because he sold his birthright. And the consequence was now to make him a slave to his brother. Esau lost the blessing and inheritance of his birthright. But now, to continue to live forever as a slave to his brother, it was up to the choices he was going to make. The word “dominion” in the phrase “…when you shall have the dominion” as used in the King James Translation is not the same Hebrew word “râdâh” (rule, subjugate, reign, tread down, overtake) as used in Genesis 1:26, 28. The word dominion used in Genesis 27:40 is from the Hebrew word “rûd”, which means “to disconsolate”. It speaks of a person becoming discomforted in a place or being restless in a way of thinking. Esau’s past mistakes and choices had consequentially placed him in this position of slavery. His background and past have created a limitations for his future. But if only he shall awaken himself from anything keeping him in that position, he will have to break the yoke from his neck and live free. Esau had the choice to remain bitter, crushed, defeated, disappointed, and enslaved, or he would shake himself out of such a state to carve a path into blessings for himself.
And all that Esau needed to break free was to forgive and love Jacob.
Esau wasn’t to live in the pain of the past. The more he envied and lived bitterly towards Jacob, the more he subjected himself to the yoke of his brother. Esau did forgive Jacob and continued to prosper, and they both flourished as well (Genesis 33:4-16). It was the descendants of Esau (Edomites) who continued in the foolishness of bitterness and envy of Israel (descendants of Jacob) that led to their destruction. However, the point basically is this: if even Esau had a way of escape from his past failure, much more you? Living in limitation and struggle is a choice. You have to make a decision to take advantage of the power and victory of Christ at work in you. He has supplied great faith into you so that you will walk in the reality of an overcomer. Don’t settle for the limitations around you. Don’t think according to your background or where you live. Don’t make decisions according to how you feel.
Jesus came to break all limitations! And greater is He that is in you than He that is in the world.
Shake yourself from every yoke of the mind and of the heart. Live above all limitations. DIG DEEPER(Luke 4:18; Psalm 147:5; Luke 21:15; 2 Corinthians 12:9) WE PRAYWe pray that our hearts shall not settle or be comforted under any force of limitation to our destiny. But we shall live by the limitless ability of God. BIBLE READING IN THE YEAR 20261 YEAR PLAN Ezekiel 37–40 2 YEARS PLAN Isaiah 2–3 DECLARE THESE WORDS:– I refuse to allow myself to settle or be comforted under any force of limitation to my destiny. – I live by the limitless ability of God. – I refuse to make decisions according to how I feel, I am led by the Lord. – I shake myself from every yoke of the mind and heart. – I live above all limitations. Oh glory to God. Thank you Lord Jesus!

title: EPISODE 1331 - STOP THE SELF PITY-PARTY
content:
CHRIST COMMONWEALTH-COMMUNITY The Love-Life Agency Download PDF God wants to write His story through your life. Exercise the courage to pursue your LION this year. The set time is now, dare to manifest greater results. Hallelujah! Apostle Bennie Author Monday, 14th September, 2026 STOP THE SELF PITY-PARTY “For everyone born of God is victorious and overcomes the world; and this is the victory that has conquered and overcome the world—our [continuing, persistent] faith [in Jesus the Son of God].” 1 John 5:4 (Amplified Bible) While talking about the “heroes of faith”, the author of the book of Hebrews mentioned Gideon. “How much more do I need to say? It would take too long to recount the stories of the faith of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and all the prophets.” Hebrews 11:32 (NLT) To have Gideon’s name among “heroes of faith” is an evidence that you are only celebrated and remembered for your victory and not your limitations. No one will celebrate your insecurities and low self-regard. No one will remember you for feeling worthless. Without God’s intervention, Gideon would have remained subjugated by his mental limitations. And Israel wouldn’t have experienced him as a great leader and deliverer.
Until you stop the self-pity party, destinies are going to be destroyed.
Awakening from the “worthlessness” feelings will make you a blessing to many. Gideon did struggle with an inferiority complex. He defined himself by his family status. He struggled with insecurity, self-doubt, and worthlessness. When God came to him, He referred to him as “…a mighty man of valor”. His trauma, self-doubt, low self-regard and the fear of the Midianites made him question even the thought that God was with the Israelites. Gideon also doubted that he was a mighty man. While the Lord saw him as a mighty man of valor, a man of great strength to save or deliver Israel, he saw himself as insignificant. “But Gideon said to Him, “Please Lord, how am I to rescue Israel? Behold, my family is the least [significant] in Manasseh, and I am the youngest (smallest) in my father’s house.” Judges 6:15 (Amplified Bible) This Gideon, who disregarded himself, felt to be the weakest among the weak (considering his family background), irrelevant, insignificant and worthless to lead Israel, became a hero of faith. Even his faith became a testimony for those of the New Testament (and generations yet unborn). Gideon would have remained worthless if he had not yielded to the word of the Lord.
It is not how you feel about yourself, it is what God says about you.
The word of God is the mirror of God, which brings you to the knowledge of your true self. Gideon was able to break free from his insecurities and low self-regard because of the revelational light of God. Don’t think you are the first to have self-doubt. You have seen Abraham and Sarah, and also Gideon. Even Jeremiah the Prophet had insecurities. Here is his personal testimony: “Ah, Lord GOD,” I said, “I surely do not know how to speak, for I am only a child!” But the LORD told me: “Do not say, ‘I am only a child.’ For to everyone I send you, you must go, and all that I command you, you must speak. Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you,” declares the LORD.…” Jeremiah 1:6-8 (Berean Study Bible) Moses doubted his eloquence to speak before Pharaoh. He disregarded himself because he was slow of speech and tongue. (Exodus 4:10-12). Later, when he submitted his thoughts to the word of the Lord, he led Israel out of captivity.
Many lives will not be impacted or transformed when you keep doubting yourself and what God has called you to do.
No matter the insecurities, the doubts and the weakness you feel, this is what the Lord is saying to you: “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” (2 Corinthians 12:9). Hallelujah! title: EPISODE 1332 - LIVE FREE
content:
CHRIST COMMONWEALTH-COMMUNITY The Love-Life Agency Download PDF The Holy Spirit supplies your life with rivers of living waters, which causes you to blossom in all things. Do you want to flourish beyond measure? Let the Holy Spirit take over your soul. Shalom. Apostle Bennie Author Tuesday, 15th September, 2026 LIVE FREE “For everyone born of God is victorious and overcomes the world; and this is the victory that has conquered and overcome the world—our [continuing, persistent] faith [in Jesus the Son of God].” 1 John 5:4 (Amplified Bible) Sarah conquered and overcame biological limitations by faith in God. Laughter of doubt was her initial response to the message of the Lord that she was going to give birth to a son. Even her husband Abraham had that same response. “Then Abraham bowed down to the ground, but he laughed to himself in disbelief. “How could I become a father at the age of 100?” he thought. “And how can Sarah have a baby when she is ninety years old?” (Genesis 17:17) But the Lord brought them to the consciousness of His power. He asked them, “Is anything too hard for the Lord?…” (Genesis 18:14). Is your answer “yes” to the above question? I doubt you will even think that way. Nothing is too hard for the Lord. This gives you the advantage. The initial response of Abraham and Sarah wasn’t just based on doubt, but the display of their self-doubt, low self-regard or low self-esteem and insecurities. Their laughter was the voice of their low self-esteem and insecurities. These are also limitations to greatness.
Low self-esteem, self-regard, and insecurities have limited people from receiving and enjoying their blessings.
Are you struggling with low self-esteem? Has that also become your limitation? Faith is your way out of that limitation. People don’t think low self-esteem is a limitation.  They think that’s how they are and their way of adjusting to society.  No one is born with low self-esteem. People are cultured into that state of mind. Break free from it! You are reading this now, and you are really struggling with low self-esteem or low self-regard and insecurities. These have influenced you not to dare to step into your purpose and calling. It makes you undermine your potential and prefer to hide or dim your light. Because of your sense of insecurity, you are afraid to be corrected. You take every correction as an attack. You are afraid to make mistakes because of the thoughts of others. And how you were a target of bullying and mockery. You are not growing into the best version of yourself because you are scared to be in the limelight. You live caged and reduced, yet cry for liberation in your soul and don’t know how! You feel intimidated when you meet others doing great things. All you do in secret is to cry, cuddle the feeling of worthlessness, nurture envy whenever you see what others are achieving. Do you know you increase your low self-regard and insecurities as you continue to think and live that way?
Low self-regard and insecurities are proof that you have not allowed the Word of God to influence your heart, thus, you are not living by faith.
You may not be the one responsible for the development of that low self-esteem, but it is your responsibility to continue in it or to step out of it. Make a decision that you are going to live free from these projectiles of darkness. Maybe growing up as a child: – you were ridiculed by almost everyone. – you didn’t receive love, affection, family warmth and positive affirmations. – you were traumatised, abused and neglected. – you couldn’t fit into your sphere, or the circles you found yourself and were bullied by your peers. – you were constantly criticised and compared to others. – poor academic performance from early childhood education to basic school. Even Now: – you experience poor academic performance and poor work performance. – you feel isolated by society. – you are always criticised by others, including family, friends, employers and mentors. Maybe you are even struggling with: – abusive relationships – not meeting expectations – societal pressures – social media “troll” and comparison – stage fright, anxiety or fear and chronic stress. These things erode self-regard or self-esteem and induce a sense of inner worthlessness. It leads to a feeling of inadequacy. It amplifies mental disorders.
Instead of allowing yourself to be continuously brandished and decimated or pulverised by these experiences, take a stand on the word of God.
The word of God builds you up as an edifice and makes you rise above these inner limitations by faith. Faith is living out the dominion of light. And faith is produced in you through the revelational light of the Word. When the light of the Word shone in the heart of Abraham and Sarah, they rose from the mental limitation of barrenness into the possibility of becoming the source of many nations. Make a decision today that you are going to break free from every limitation. Hallelujah! title: EPISODE 1333 - HIGHLY ESTEEM YOUR LEADERS IN LOVE
content:
CHRIST COMMONWEALTH-COMMUNITY The Love-Life Agency Download PDF We are not of this world. We are not in agreement with this world. You are not a sinner. You are a son of God. You are in fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ, our Lord. GLORY TO GOD! Apostle Bennie Author Wednesday, 16th September, 2026 HIGHLY ESTEEM YOUR LEADERS IN LOVE“and [we ask that you appreciate them and] hold them in the highest esteem in love because of their work [on your behalf]. Live in peace with one another.” 1 Thessalonians 5:13 (Amplified Bible)  You don’t honour your leaders by doing what pleases you or what you claim to be right. You don’t honour your leaders by doing your best. The Bible provides practical things to do to appreciate and honour your leaders.To appreciate and honour your leader is a demonstration of the character of the Spirit. And it’s essential for the edification and growth of the Church, even for the expansion of the Kingdom. Sometimes people make assertions that members (or the flock) overly esteem their leaders. Their leaders are not God and should not be idolized. 
Get this, members whose hearts are knitted to God will not make idols out of their leaders. Leaders whose interest is to serve the purpose of God for His people wouldn’t seek such idolization.
However, Apostle Paul’s words in 1 Thessalonians 5:13 explain the extent leaders must be honoured. This is how it’s put in the King James version: “And we beseech you, brethren, to know them which labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you; and to esteem them very highly in love for their work’s sake. And be at peace among yourselves.” 1 Thessalonians 5:12-13 (KJV) “…and to esteem them very highly in love…” This expression is greatly enthusiastic and overwhelming in Greek. The words (esteem, very, and highly), as translated from the Greek language, are rich in their individual meanings; much more when they are all put together in one sentence. When you get to understand the meaning of each word, you may think it’s a repetition of an idea in Greek. However, Paul the apostle usually puts similar words in the same sentence, not just as emphasis, but to help explain the extent or degree of the point he is making. To “esteem them very highly in love” is as Paul the apostle being verbose in the phrase “…exceedingly abundantly above all…” Remember, I said, Paul the apostle writes in such a manner to explain the depths of the inspiration he has received. – The word “esteem” (hēgeomai) means to consider the influence of a leader. This word is only used for high-ranking leaders or rulers.  – These four-letter words “Very” have been watered down by some people in their daily usage. But it means more than “exact, actual or precise”.  Very is an emphasis of a high degree or an exceedingly high degree of a matter. The Greek word for “Very” is “huper”, which means to place above, to go beyond or across or that which is superior to more than. Anything above more than. It suggests superiority or excess. The root word for hype or hyper can be traced to the Greek word “huper”. Have you ever been told “you Hype your leader too much?”. Interestingly, no one speaks against the idea that you over hype your favourite footballer or movie character or politician. Yet the moment you begin to “hype” your Church leader, they call you names. I suppose, so far, you have an idea of what Paul the apostle is saying about honouring your leader. – Now look at the word, “HIGHLY”.It’s from the Greek word “perissos”. It also means superabundant (in quantity) or superior (in quality); It means preeminence, exceeding, abundantly above, more abundantly, advantage, very highly, vehemently beyond, measure more, superfluous. Do you now get the degree at which you must demonstrate honor to your leader? How well do you honor your leader? Now you don’t honour your leader because of his or her age. You don’t honour your leader because of his title or position. Paul the Apostle was clear on this: you honour your leader because of the work and sacrifice they make for you. You don’t honour your leader because of his or her financial status or intellectual capacity.
A leader whose business is the welfare of your spirit and soul must be vehemently and superabundantly esteemed, and hyped beyond the degree the people of the world have set.
The people of the world feel agitated when the saints exceedingly esteem their spiritual leaders. Don’t be shy to highly esteem your leader, especially in this time and age where people are looking down on Church Leaders. There are genuine Church leaders who have sacrificed their interests for the edification of the Church. Selah. Stay glued for tomorrow’s episode.DIG DEEPER(1 Timothy 5:17; 1 Corinthians  16:15-16; Philippians 2:28-30; 1 Peter 5:5) WE PRAYWe pray that we shall highly esteem the leaders the Lord has set over us, and with the responsibility to nurture us in the faith. BIBLE READING IN THE YEAR 20261 YEAR PLAN Ezekiel 47–48, Daniel 1 2 YEARS PLAN Isaiah 6 DECLARE THESE WORDS:– I set my heart right to practically honour my leaders today.– I walk in honor towards my Leader. – I  don’t dishonor the authorities God has set over me. – I refuse to be ungrateful towards my leader. – I honor my Leader with my treasure, time and finances. – I demonstrate honor towards my leader in all things. Thank you Lord for my Leader.

title: EPISODE 1334 - FORGET NOT ALL HIS BENEFITS
content:
CHRIST COMMONWEALTH-COMMUNITY The Love-Life Agency Download PDF Apostle Bennie Author Thursday, 17th September, 2026 FORGET NOT ALL HIS BENEFITS “Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all His benefits” Psalm 103:2 (KJV) This Psalm of David is a rich and interesting Psalm. It unveils one crucial thing you should do daily as a believer in Christ: remembering and exhorting yourself with the things which the LORD has done. Whilst Job was afflicted by the adversary to curse God, David was speaking to himself to BLESS THE LORD. David didn’t live his entire life without challenges. He had victories in all his battles. However, he failed in moral battles; experienced betrayals; he was always on the run in his youth. Some years into David’s reign, his own son Absalom conspired and rose against him. His life was always threatened and attacked. From being a wanted hero or soon-to-be king on the run, he later became the wanted king.
Yet in his reflective moments, he exhorts himself to BLESS THE LORD and not FORGET HIS BENEFITS.
He didn’t invest time in recounting defeats. Firstly, you must learn to exhort or speak right to yourself. And just in case you may be wondering what to speak to yourself about, get into Psalm 103. And this devotional, Machaira with Apostle Bennie, is here to bring you into the understanding of the word. Every episode draws your attention to the rich realities you have in God through Christ. As you seem to be overwhelmed by challenges, failures and pains, you are likely to forget the glorious things the Lord has done. There are believers who don’t even recall anything good from God when they look into their lives. They even live with a conclusive mindset that God is the source or cause of their sufferings. The adversary takes delight in this. He wants you to think and accept that God doesn’t want anything good for your life. That is how he attacks the faith of the believer. Meanwhile these are God’s own words to you: “For I know the plans I have for you,” says the LORD. “They are plans for good and not for disaster, to give you a future and a hope.” Jeremiah 29:11 (NLT) In your most reflective moments what do you set your heart on? Do you spend time thinking about the mistakes you’ve made, your failures, disappointments and defeats?
Beloved, in all your reflective moments, BLESS THE LORD!
You have to intentionally talk to yourself to BLESS THE LORD. You have to saturate your mind, will and emotions with the reality of who God is and all that He has done. David didn’t only speak to himself to BLESS the Lord, he also conscientised his heart of the things he has to set on his mind. To exhort his soul not to forget the benefits of the Lord shows David’s intentionality. The biggest challenge and limitation in your faith walk is forgetfulness of the Lord’s benefits. Until you begin to walk in the remembrance of the Lord’s benefits, you will be robbed by the adversary. “Bless the Lord, O my soul, And forget not all His benefits:” In this Psalm of David, he went on to articulate the specific benefits he must not forget.
He kept his heart in the remembrance of all that the Lord has done.
And penned them for us to have such remembrance. This was why the second verse ended with a colon (:). He further listed the benefits: No matter the happenings around you, REMEMBER that the LORD: •  forgives all your iniquities, •  heals all your diseases, •  redeems your life from destruction, •  crowns you with lovingkindness and tender mercies, •  satisfies your mouth with good things, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle’s. •  executes righteousness and justice for all who are oppressed. (See verses 3–6) This means you are not to accept in your heart that the Lord is angry with you and does not forgive you. In verse 8, he painted a picture of God’s person: “the Lord is MERCIFUL and GRACIOUS, Slow to anger, and ABOUNDING IN MERCY.” This is the consciousness you must have about God.
Don’t allow your heart to forget who He is and all His benefits.
The more you walk in the remembrance of these things, the more your heart will be delighted in blessings instead of murmuring. Selah. DIG DEEPER(Ephesians 1:3; Psalm 68:19; Psalm 9:1; Psalm 103:10; Psalm 136:1; Psalm 116:12; 1 Sam 16:7; Deuteronomy 6:12) WE PRAY We pray that our hearts shall not forget, but always be settled in the remembrance of the Graciousness of the LORD. BIBLE READING IN THE YEAR 20261 YEAR PLANDaniel 2–4 2 YEARS PLAN Isaiah 7 DECLARE THESE WORDS: – I don’t forget the graciousness of the Lord towards me. – The Lord is gracious and kind to me at all times. – I enjoy the benefits of the Lord each day. – No matter the circumstance or challenge, I don’t allow my heart to forget all the benefits of the Lord. – The Lord redeems my life daily from destruction. – The Lord heals all my diseases. – The Lord forgives all my iniquities. – The Lord crowns me with loving kindness and tender mercies. – The Lord satisfies my mouth with good things. – I am deeply loved by the Lord. Thank you Lord Jesus!

It is the haven and bastion of divine reality. Through the Church, you are nurtured, equipped and deeply rooted in truth. “Then we will no longer be like children, forever changing our minds about what we believe because someone has told us something different or has cleverly lied to us and made the lie sound like the truth.” Ephesians 4:14 (TLB). However, the light of the truth cannot be comprehended by any dimension of darkness.  Don’t allow your experiences of some people within the Church to corrupt your love for the Lord, and then move you away from the community of the Church. title: EPISODE 1336 - BE BOLD ABOUT THE GOSPEL
content:
CHRIST COMMONWEALTH-COMMUNITY The Love-Life Agency Download PDF Don’t look away from the reality of Jesus. He is God! He is Eternal and His saving Grace is everlasting! His blood which purchased you is a divine blood. It is an eternal blood. JESUS IS GOD! This is the gospel. Hallelujah Apostle Bennie Author Saturday, 19th September, 2026 BE BOLD ABOUT THE GOSPEL “For unlike so many, we are not peddlers of God’s Word who water down the message. We are those sent from God with pure motives, who speak in the sight of God from our union with Christ.” 2 Corinthians 2:17 (TPT) The gospel is the goodnews of Jesus. In the Kingdom of our Lord Jesus, there are no two gospels; the gospel is one.
There is no goodnews in the universe which is as good as the glorious news of Jesus.
The gospel of our Lord Jesus is the consistent revelation of God in Christ Jesus. It is the declaration of the supply of God’s love and demonstration of His graciousness. The gospel unveils how God has justified all who received Jesus and has made them righteous in Christ. It is the communication of God’s eternal forgiveness. The gospel says, you are not saved by your works or self-efforts. But you are saved by grace through faith in Christ Jesus. “For it was only through this wonderful grace that we believed in him. Nothing we did could ever earn this salvation, for it was the gracious gift from God that brought us to Christ! So no one will ever be able to boast, for salvation is never a reward for good works or human striving.” Ephesians 2:8-9 (TPT) To preach that we are saved by grace, however, we need our works to preserve our salvation, is to water down the good news of Jesus.

Jesus did not die for you because you were righteous. He died for all men when we were yet sinners. The only price which was paid for the salvation of men was the blood of Jesus. Though salvation is not cheap, God has freely made it available for us through Christ Jesus. To preach the gospel for self-gain or selfish interest is to peddle or water down the gospel of Jesus. That which the Lord has done is complete! It does not need additives or your sentiments to make it whole. Jesus did a finished work through His death and resurrection.
When your goal of preaching the gospel is also to enrich your selfish ambition, you may have to preach a mixed gospel which also another gospel.

title: EPISODE 1336 - DOES GOD SPEAK THROUGH VISIONS AND DREAMS?
content:
CHRIST COMMONWEALTH-COMMUNITY The Love-Life Agency Download PDF Apostle Bennie Author Saturday, 19th September, 2026  DOES GOD SPEAK THROUGH VISIONS AND DREAMS?“And he said, “Hear my words: If there is a prophet among you, I the Lord make myself known to him in a vision; I speak with him in a dream. Not so with my servant Moses. He is faithful in all my house. With him I speak mouth to mouth, clearly, and not in riddles, and he beholds the form of the Lord. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?”   Numbers 12:6-8 (ESV) A vision is an evocative impression or a revelational imprint of images or pictures in a person’s mind that articulates a hidden event or situation. Meanwhile, a dream is a projected image and imaginary transaction or deep thoughts that engage a person’s soul and mind while asleep. A vision may sometimes be experienced even with the optical eyes and not just in the mind. There are times when the physical eyes are enabled to see literally into the spirit world to behold hidden things, even as a person still sees natural things. Discussion on these items is important because believers do have such experiences often. And as a believer, you must have a proper understanding of such issues. Some are careful to engage in this kind of conversation and even don’t open themselves up to receive visions because of the fear of getting into error.
As long as you submit your mind and thoughts to the revelation of the Word of God, your experiences will be guided by the authority of the Word.
Apart from dreams and visions, there is also what is referred to as Trance. Dreams, Visions and Trances are biblical. Most people confuse these three experiences and use them interchangeably. Especially between a vision and a trance. In Acts 10, you will find how two people had two unique prophetic experiences. Cornelius was an Italian Centurion, who was a devout man and had a vision, which led to his conversion. In that same chapter, Peter also had a prophetic revelation. But the experience of Peter the apostle was different from that of Cornelius. Cornelius had an open vision while Peter had a trance. “a devout man of extraordinary character who worshiped God and prayed regularly, together with all his family. He also had a heart for the poor and gave generously to help them. One afternoon about three o’clock, he had an open vision and saw the angel of God appear right in front of him, calling out his name, “Cornelius!” Startled, he was overcome with fear by the sight of the angel. He asked, “What do you want, Lord?” The angel said, “All of your prayers and your generosity to the poor have ascended before God as an eternal offering.” Acts 10:2-4 (TPT). This wasn’t a dream. He literally saw the angel by way of vision. His eyes were opened to see and to hear. The Greek word for vision in this context is “horama” which means that which is seen. It is to have a view of a spectacular moment. Cornelius’ vision wasn’t an imagination and not just a mental picture. This means visions cannot be limited to a mental imprint. They are both mental imprints and the capturing of a live event in the spirit realm. People mostly experience these while in prayer. The place of prayer is a place of visions and spectacular prophetic experiences.
Whenever you pray or delve into the word of God, your spirit ascends to see far beyond the normal and optics.
After this amazing vision of Cornelius, God quickly sent a prophetic message to Peter to help have confirmation and to receive the message from Cornelius. “The next day around noon, as Cornelius’ men were approaching Joppa, Peter went up to the flat roof of the house to pray. He was hungry and wanted to eat, but while lunch was being prepared he fell into a trance and entered into another realm. As the heavenly realm opened up, he saw something resembling a large linen tablecloth that descended from above, being let down to the earth by its four corners. As it floated down he saw that it held many kinds of four-footed animals, reptiles, and wild birds. A voice said to him, “Peter, go and prepare them to be eaten.” Peter replied, “There’s no way I could do that, Lord, for I’ve never eaten anything forbidden or impure according to our Jewish laws.” The voice spoke again. “Nothing is unclean if God declares it to be clean.” The vision was repeated three times. Then suddenly the linen sheet was snatched back up into heaven. Peter was so stunned by the vision that he couldn’t stop wondering about what all it meant. Meanwhile, Cornelius’ men had learned where Peter was staying and at that same moment were standing outside the gate. They called out to those in the house, “Is this where Simon, the Rock, is staying?” As Peter was in deep thought, trying to interpret the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Go downstairs now, for three men are looking for you. Don’t hesitate to go with them, because I have sent them.” Acts 10:9-20 (TPT) Peter’s experience was not referred to as a dream or a vision. It was referred to as a Trance. The Greek word for Trance is, “ekstasis”. Which means the displacement of the mind or bewilderment. It is used to describe a moment of ecstasy. It is a state where a person is caught up into a different realm. John the apostle had this experience several times while writing the book of Revelation. Most of what he referred to as “I was in the spirit” were trances. You transit from one state into a different realm, while you are physically in the same location but your inner man has travelled into a different realm. It is a moment of awe and amazement.
During trance, one can also see a vision.
Thus trance goes together with a vision. Within every trance, there is a vision. God is able to communicate with the believer through such means to enforce his message. Yet all these experiences are subject to the governing rule or constitution of His word. There is no experience of such which transcends the light of the Word of God. I call you blessed. Shalom! Thank you Lord for the gift of your word!
